function_question: How does nature cool a place without energy?

opening.text: There was a girl called Sara, 14, who sat on her city's youth council and loved her busy street.
Sara walked through the shady park, then onto her own block, where by noon the pavement felt like an oven.
A heat wave hit. The street was 5 °C hotter than the park, and her elderly neighbour couldn't sleep. "The council wants a plan by Friday," Sara said. "But we can't give everyone air conditioning."

card.problem: The street is 5 °C hotter than the park
card.goal: A street model that stays cooler in the sun
card.rules: No electricity, and prove it with thermometers

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. Sara's street is 5 °C hotter than the park, and the council wants a plan that uses no electricity. Can you help her? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some designers already have a hunch about cooling a street. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Nature has no air conditioners, yet life thrives in deserts and savannas. Tap each card to see how four heroes beat the heat!
guide.design_secret: Here's what all four heroes have in common…
guide.skill: Scientists test one variable at a time. Which surface will be hottest after 30 minutes? Predict first, then read the thermometers.
guide.sketch: Draw your street as a cross-section and label every strategy with the hero that inspired it.
guide.build_and_test: Put your model and the plain control side by side in full sun. Read both thermometers every 10 minutes for 30 minutes. How many degrees cooler is yours?
guide.retry_tip: Real engineers find out what each part is worth. Take ONE strategy out, test again, and see how much the temperature changes.
guide.ending: And ever since then, Sara's block has shady trees and cool white roofs, and her neighbour sleeps well even on the hottest nights!

quick_check.question: After 30 minutes in the sun, the plain model reads 41 °C and Sara's model reads 36.5 °C. How much cooler is Sara's model?
quick_check.right: Right! 41 minus 36.5 is 4.5 °C. That's almost the whole gap between the street and the park!
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. Subtract Sara's reading from the control: 41 minus 36.5.

clue_cards.name: Tree canopy
clue_cards.trick: Its leaves shade the ground and release water vapour through tiny pores.
clue_cards.does: Shade plus evaporation can keep the ground 10 to 20 °C cooler than sunny asphalt.

clue_cards.name: Termite mound
clue_cards.trick: A tall mound full of tunnels and chimneys.
clue_cards.does: Daily warming and cooling push air through the nest, so it gets fresh air with no fan.

clue_cards.name: Saharan silver ant
clue_cards.trick: Triangular silver hairs cover its body.
clue_cards.does: They reflect sunlight and shed heat, keeping it 5 to 10 °C cooler on sand hotter than 60 °C.

clue_cards.name: Kalahari ground squirrel
clue_cards.trick: It flips its bushy tail over its back like a sunshade.
clue_cards.does: Carrying its own shade lets it keep feeding in the midday sun for longer.

predict.prompt: Traps heat or keeps it cool? Predict first!

items.label: A black asphalt road in full sun
A row of leafy street trees

predict.explain: Dark surfaces absorb most of the sunlight that hits them and turn it into heat. White surfaces reflect much more of it, and trees add shade plus cooling from evaporating water.

lab.title: The surface heat lab

options: Black card with a damp cloth

tool.name: Biomimicry Design Spiral
tool.intro: The Biomimicry Design Spiral is the process real biomimicry designers use. It has 6 steps, and you loop round it again and again. Today you'll learn the first 3: Define, Biologize and Discover.

parts.name: Define
parts.what: Say exactly what your design must do, for whom, and where.
parts.example: ☂️ Keep one person dry in heavy rain and strong wind, without flipping inside out.
parts.starter: Sara's street must stay cooler for the people who…

parts.name: Biologize
parts.what: Turn that job into a nature question: How does nature…?
parts.example: ☂️ How does nature shed water and survive strong gusts?
parts.starter: How does nature keep a place cool without…

parts.name: Discover
parts.what: Find living things that are experts at it, and how they do it.
parts.example: ☂️ A lotus leaf beads rain off with tiny waxy bumps, and a palm leaf bends in the wind instead of snapping.
parts.starter: One expert at staying cool is… and it does it by…

reflection.question: Which nature trick cooled your street the most?
